before.name: Uniform geometric probability
before.description: For a uniformly chosen point in a positive finite segment or measurable plane region, probability is favorable length or area divided by total. State uniformity and parameter domains, and handle boundaries by their measure.
criteria: Translate the event into a measurable favorable region under the specified uniform model.
Compute its measure ratio with the correct parameter cases and probability range.
before.scopeRationale: Classical probability is explicitly finite and equally likely by sample point. A random cut is continuous; one cannot count uncountably many points by the finite m/n rule. The omitted x domain still needs a piecewise answer.
before.aliasDecision: Retain neighboring node identities and grade scopes. This proposal changes the mathematical task class, not merely its English label. No automatic alias or redirect.

catalogRefinementLineage.reason: Uniform volume probability is the same normalized-measure construction as uniform length/area probability, but the current B description explicitly stops at plane regions. Add solids and arc measure explicitly, retain positive finite measure, and do not infer coordinate independence from marginal uniformity. No new volume-probability ID is useful.

before.name: Elimination from public statements of uncertainty
before.nameZh: 公开不确定陈述下的候选消元
before.description: Given finitely many possible worlds and each participant's private observation, track what each can distinguish. A truthful claim of not knowing the complete world removes singleton observation classes before the next public announcement.
criteria: Construct each participant observation class from the currently possible worlds, not the original possibilities after later announcements.
Apply announcements in order and identify which private observations still permit more than one possible world.
before.scopeRationale: The static finite-constraint procedure does not explicitly model different private observations or public updates. The task demands exactly this extra procedure, not a new integer equation method.
before.aliasDecision: Keep neighboring scopes distinct. No automatic alias or redirect is proposed.
before.alternativeResolution: A transparent table of candidate triples and successive multiplicities is equivalent. No modal-logic syntax or general epistemic-logic framework is required.

nativeScopeAudit.reason: Static constraints enumerate possible worlds but do not update observation classes after public announcements of ignorance. The recomputed singleton-class elimination is the actual additional reasoning, and a finite table gives a complete elementary representation.

catalogRefinementLineage.reason: The current C procedure only tests whether a whole world is known. Warranted knowledge of a proposition is the natural observation-class generalization and retains the complete-world uncertainty case. The score question still needs its warranted-thought interpretation; extending a catalog definition cannot cure that source ambiguity.

before.name: Center distances for tangent spheres
before.nameZh: 相切球的球心距离条件
before.description: Externally tangent spheres of positive radii have center distance equal to the radius sum. A sphere tangent to a plane has center-to-plane distance equal to its radius. Use the side of the plane to locate the centers.
criteria: Translate external sphere contact and sphere-plane contact into the correct center-distance equations.
Use center geometry to recover a requested height or separation, distinguishing a center height from the top of the sphere.
before.scopeRationale: The actual sphere scope identifies its radius; the circle-position node concerns coplanar circles. Pythagoras and centroid ratios compute the height only after contact is translated to spatial center distances. Those contact facts are not supplied in the task or existing criteria.
before.aliasDecision: Keep neighboring scopes distinct. No automatic alias or redirect is proposed.
before.alternativeResolution: A local proof from the triangle inequality for sphere contact and a perpendicular radius for plane contact is enough. No sphere packing theorem or general internal tangency classification is proposed.

nativeScopeAudit.reason: Circle-position criteria concern coplanar circles, not spheres and planes. Equal center-distance equations must be established before Pythagoras or centroid geometry can calculate the height. Positive radii, external tangency and the selected side of the plane remain explicit.
